_source: CW_Issues 29-Jul-2026 rows 15-24, authored on the analyst's instruction of 30-Jul (Subrato: 'work on all these').
_scope: Client NextPower, target object Customer. Seeded as client-scoped rules so every Customer conversion for this client inherits them, which is what the 'Describe a rule' box does when an analyst types one — this is the same thing, pre-typed.
_column_spellings: Each source column is a LIST of candidate spellings, not one string. The rules were dictated in prose ('StartDate, falling back to datecreated') and the extract's real headers are whatever NetSuite exported; a single guessed spelling binds to nothing and fails silently. COALESCE skips a column that is missing or blank, and a CASE_WHEN branch on an absent column reads as blank and falls through — so listing every plausible spelling is safe and a wrong guess costs nothing. Confirm against your extract and delete the ones that do not apply.
_open_questions: CW #23 as written gives 'NXT000001' (3 + 6 digits) for an organization but 'NXT00001_C1' (3 + 5 digits) for a PERSON. Two different key widths in one column is unusual and looks like a transcription slip. Implemented exactly as written — variant width 5 — so it matches your sheet; change variant.width to 6 if both should be the same length.

CW #23 also contradicts section 10.6, where auto-generated key numbers were REMOVED on your instruction because a manufactured unique value made genuine duplicates look distinct. Your 30-Jul instruction overrides that. Two safeguards are built in: the sequence is assigned at finalize, AFTER duplicate decisions, and preserve_source means a real source key always wins. Do NOT add Party Number to the duplicate-identity columns.

CW #17 was specified as depending on WHICH source column fed Phone Number. Implemented on the per-row evidence instead — mobile column populated means MOBILE, fax column populated means FAX — because that is decidable per row and provenance is not. Confirm the two source columns.
CW #19 and #24 were both marked 'awaiting data' on your sheet. The rules are authored and will apply the moment the file arrives; they cannot be verified against real values until then.

rules.description: Account Established Date takes StartDate, falling back to datecreated when StartDate is blank.
EMAIL when an email address is present on the row, otherwise PHONE.
MOBILE when the mobile source column carries the number, FAX when the fax column does.
rules._note: Mobile is tested before fax deliberately: a row carrying both is a mobile number with a fax on file, not a fax line. Default is blank rather than a guess — Phone Line Type is a coded column and inventing a code fails the value-set check with no clue why.

rules.description: BILL_TO where Default Billing is set, SHIP_TO where DefaultShipping is set.
rules._note: NetSuite exports these as T/F or checkbox columns, so notblank would also fire on a literal 'F'. If your extract carries F for false, change op to eq with value T — check one row before generating.

CONCAT falls back to the incoming value when EVERY input is missing, rather than emitting a bare '_'. That guard exists because Supplier Site once shipped 8,561 rows of the literal '-' into a required unique key when neither input column existed.

rules.description: PERSON when a first or last name is present, otherwise ORGANIZATION.
Append _b on a bill-to row and _s on a ship-to row.

BILL_TO on a bill-to row, SHIP_TO on a ship-to row.
Unique sequence NXT000001; a PERSON gets the NXT00001_C1 form.
